message: OVD-934 AC2 asks for a test that a new SHA triggers a re-screen; no repo test pushes a new head and asserts a Jev call (the closest, line 644, covers the inverse: a stale SHA skips the marker). QA probe P2 shows the behaviour works (new head: Jev called, marker written on the new SHA). Add the test. Jev triage: real (not flaky/infra).

OVD-934 AC1 and fix item 3 name the row fields cache_hit and head_sha and ask for tokens; rows log marker_hit and sha and carry no token count. Jev triage: real; fix in code (log cache_hit and head_sha, keep aliases, add tokens or null). Same meaning (second same-SHA screen logs marker_hit=true with 1 Jev call, probe P1), but the field names differ from the issue and tokens are not logged.

The default CLI now writes a jev-screen success commit status to GitHub as optomachina on every accepted screen. It is not a required check (branch protection requires ci and provider-go-live only, and qa-handoff gate.mjs counts only required checks), but any all-green helper over commit statuses, including the OVD-845 gate, must exclude jev-screen.
The new marker module is not on the sensitive-path list (docs/sensitive-paths.json covers scripts/jev-pr-screen* only); tracked as OVD-939 C2.
The #743 duplicate came from screen.py, which does not read or write the marker, so dedupe across both callers (issue fix item 1) holds only after screen.py is retired; tracked as OVD-940.

When an injected marker writer throws or returns a free-text reason, the warning echoes it after sanitizeToken, which redacts only TYPESAFE_API_KEY (probe P5). The real GitHub writer returns fixed reason codes, so no token reaches logs today; keep reasons to fixed codes.
